desc:
An undirected network has n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1. It is given as an adjacency list: adj[u] lists the neighbours of node u in a fixed order. Every connection is two-way, so v appears in adj[u] exactly when u appears in adj[v].

A copier starts at node start and explores the network breadth first: it takes the earliest discovered node that has not been expanded yet, and looks at that node's neighbours in the order they are listed, discovering each neighbour it has not seen before. Return the nodes in the order in which they are discovered, beginning with start. Nodes that cannot be reached from start are not part of the answer.
constraints: The total length of all neighbour lists is at most 12,000
Connections are symmetric, with no self loops and no repeated neighbour inside one list
hints: The order depends on which node is expanded next, so you need a first-in, first-out structure.
Put start in a queue and mark it seen. Repeatedly remove the front node, record it, and walk through its neighbours in the listed order.
Mark a neighbour as seen at the moment you add it to the queue, not when you remove it, so no node is queued twice. The order in which nodes leave the queue is the discovery order.
editorial: This is plain breadth-first search with one detail: the neighbour order is given, so the result is completely determined. Keep a queue and a seen array. Pop the front node u, append it to the answer, then scan adj[u] from left to right and push every neighbour that is not yet seen, marking it seen immediately.

Because a node is marked when it is queued, each node enters the queue once, and the queue releases nodes in exactly the order they were discovered. Every node and every neighbour-list entry is touched once, so the work is linear in the size of the input. A recursive depth-first version would give a different order (and risks deep recursion on a 3,000-node path), so use the queue.
solution:
from collections import deque


def discoveryOrder(adj, start):
    seen = [False] * len(adj)
    seen[start] = True
    order = []
    q = deque([start])
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        order.append(u)
        for v in adj[u]:
            if not seen[v]:
                seen[v] = True
                q.append(v)
    return order
